subject: Private inference performance runway & action plan
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Samir Bose <samir@brightbridge.ai>, Leah Park <leah.park@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private inference performance runway & action plan

Hi Samir / Leah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the performance/Networking handoff for your private (VPC) deployment. I captured the numbers you said would be meaningful for your product team and added a couple of pragmatic acceptance checks we typically run on our side.

Summary of targets (customer stated goals):
- Streaming tail-latency (P95): <= 150ms end-to-end per token for 1–2 concurrent client streams
- Streaming tail-latency (P99): <= 400ms under target concurrency
- Synchronous request latency (P95): <= 120ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens)
- Throughput target: sustained 500 requests/sec across the cluster; burst up to 900 rps for 30s
- Concurrency: steady-state 150 concurrent streams, spike handling to 300 with graceful degradation
- Token throughput: goal ~30–50 tokens/sec per connection depending on model size/config

Network considerations we need from you to validate the above:
1) External egress path and public egress IPs we should expect (for firewall allowlist).
2) VPN / peering topology (Transit Gateway vs direct peering) and known middleboxes (F5, HAProxy, corporate NATs).
3) NAT timeout and ephemeral port mapping behavior (we saw client-side NATs with 120s timeouts cause mid-stream disconnects).
4) Typical MTU along the path and any IPS/IDS that may reassemble/inspect TLS.
5) Any per-connection bandwidth limits (throttles) or per-IP rate-limiting in your edge.

What we'll run from our side (proposed acceptance test window):
- Traceroute + tcptraceroute + pcap from our edge to your ingress during a 2-hour window.
- Synthetic streaming test: 3 clients ramping to the target concurrency over 30 minutes while capturing P95/P99 tail-latency and packet loss.
- VPN throughput test (iperf3) across the tunnel to validate sustained 1–2 Gbps trunk capacity.
- Application-level end-to-end test with a 30s canary window and automatic fallback to hosted variant if latencies exceed thresholds.

Action items / owners (proposed):
- Samir: confirm SRE contact, provide primary egress IPs, and any existing packet-capture or firewall rules (due: 2028-03-30).
- Leah: share your preferred 2-hour window for the network tests and whether we should coordinate with your Change Control (due: 2028-03-30).
- Karthik (internal): draft acceptance criteria spreadsheet with exact measurement scripts and thresholds (I asked Karthik to own this).
- Marissa (internal): update commercial milestone to include canary window + acceptance signoff gating (prepare contract language for reserved capacity).

Attachments: sample pcap template and an acceptance-criteria workbook (I attached the template we use).

I'll wait for the SRE contact + egress IPs and then propose two slots for the 2-hour run (we prefer 10:00–12:00 PT or 20:00–22:00 PT to test different backbone loads).

Thanks —
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

> Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the performance/Networking handoff for your private (VPC) deployment.

Thanks for the clear recap, Sean. Confirming details from our side and adding a few constraints so the tests are realistic:

- Ingress sits behind an F5 LB in our AWS account (TLS termination there). We currently front with AWS ALB for some mobile workloads, but the Inference traffic will come through the F5 cluster (VIPs) you should target.
- We use AWS Transit Gateway for multi-account routing; we can peer directly if that helps, but most traffic today traverses the TGW.
- NAT timeout is configured to 300s for our egress gateways.
- No DPI appliances that break TLS, but we have an inline WAF that performs header inspection (not body).
- Ephemeral port pool is large (system default) but our egress gateways do NAT with SNAT from a small set of public IPs (I'll share them).

SRE contact: Priya Ramesh <priya.ramesh@brightbridge.ai>. Priya will coordinate packet captures and provide the list of egress IPs by end of day tomorrow.

Preferred test windows (we can do both):
- Option A: 2028-03-31 10:00–12:00 PT
- Option B: 2028-03-31 20:00–22:00 PT

We'll also attach a short network diagram and a short list of firewall rules (outbound allowlist) to the ticket. I'll loop Priya in.

Samir

samir@brightbridge.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Ramesh <priya.ramesh@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Mar 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Acceptance criteria + test plan (detailed)

Hi all —

Following up with the technical acceptance checklist we will run during the agreed window (2028-03-31). Please treat these as concrete pass/fail checks we will use for signoff.

1) Network validation (owner: BrightBridge SRE / Priya):
- Provide the set of egress IPs and confirm SNAT behavior (pass if the set is stable for the run).
- Provide a short network diagram showing TGW / F5 / ALB and CIDR blocks.
- Provide permission for a packet-capture (pcap) on the ingress VIP during the test slot.

2) Path-level tests (owner: Redwood infra / Karthik):
- tcptraceroute and mtr from our edge to the VIPs (we will collect 2 minutes baseline + 30 minutes at load).
- iperf3 test across the tunnel: target sustained 1.5 Gbps (pass if >= 1 Gbps sustained for 5 minutes).

3) Application-level streaming test (owner: Redwood SRE):
- Synthetic streaming clients: 3 geographically-distributed clients, ramp to 150 concurrent streams over 30 minutes, maintain for 30 minutes, then spike to 300 for 60s.
- Metrics collected: P50/P95/P99 latency per token, end-to-end packet retransmits, retransmit-induced reorders.
- Pass condition: P95 <= 150ms during steady-state; P99 <= 400ms. If P95 breaches by >20% for >5 minutes we fail and trigger rollback.

4) Concurrency and throughput test (owner: Redwood SRE / BrightBridge):
- Sustained 500 rps test across the cluster for 10 minutes. Burst test: 900 rps for 30s, measure queueing and tail-latency.
- Pass if sustained throughput is achieved with P95 latency targets.

5) Observability / logs (owner: BrightBridge + Redwood):
- Share flow logs and tcpdump snippet for the failure window if we see retransmits.
- Add temporary tracing headers on requests so we can correlate requests end-to-end.

6) Reporting and signoff (owner: Marissa / Priya):
- Redwood will deliver a short runbook PDF with test artifacts and a pass/fail sheet within 24 hours of the run.
- BrightBridge SRE confirms signoff or lists actionable failures within 48 hours.

Tooling note: We'll use iperf3, tcptraceroute, hping3 (for retransmit patterns), and our internal streaming harness (redwood-loadgen v2). Scripts will be shared in the Drive link.

Next steps: Priya — can you confirm the test window (you indicated both A and B are possible) and attach the egress IP list? Once we have that, Sean/Marissa will set the commercial milestone and I'll schedule the Redwood-run tests.

Thanks —
Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
